similarOrganizations.description:
Think of BEAM Devs as a tech network for developers using the BEAM through Elixir, Erlang, Gleam, and any other programming languages that adopt the BEAM VM. BEAM Devs aims to be the go-to place for everything BEAM related.

The BEAM Devs network will be a hub for developers and companies using the BEAM. Both will be able to showcase their use of the BEAM, share their experiences, and provide resources to learn and make the best of it.

The main goal of BEAM Devs is that if it is BEAM related, you should be able to find it in the BEAM Devs Network, whether learning resources, projects, libraries, case studies, stories of using it in anger, hiring full-time or contract-based, and everything in between.

On the BEAM Devs network, developers, recruiters, and companies will have their profiles defined in a structured way to make it easier to find a good match between developers, recruiters, and companies.

We hope to reshape job hunting and hiring in the BEAM ecosystem. For the future jobs board at [BEAM Devs](https://beamdevs.com), the aim is to have job descriptions made up of bullet points that are easy to read, without the need to parse the fluffy text we usually see in job descriptions. This approach will also enable both candidates and companies to specify filters to refine their search criteria, saving time for everyone involved by providing more relevant results for what they are looking for.

Once BEAM Devs becomes profitable, 10% of the annual profits will be given back to the community by sponsoring open-source BEAM projects. Everyone else will also be encouraged to support BEAM open-source projects through monetary or time contributions via a transparent program.

If this project resonates with you, then don't miss the chance to influence its direction and shape. Visit [beamdevs.com](http://beamdevs.com) now and subscribe for early access as an Alpha or Beta tester.

IEEE Transactions on Field Robotics (T-FR) by the IEEE Robotics & Automation Society (RAS) is a scholarly journal dealing with the fundamentals of robotics in unstructured and dynamic environments.  The journal focuses on methods and systems designed to operate outside the built environment, where the ambient conditions can’t be controlled and the scale is much larger than found indoors.  Articles describing research with applications in construction, forestry, agriculture, mining, subsea, intelligent highways, search and rescue, military, and space are encouraged. Papers in sensing, sensors, mechanical design, computing architectures, communication, planning, learning, and control, applied to field applications are encouraged.

Editor-in-Chief: Tim Barfoot, University of Toronto

Founding Editor: Sanjiv Singh, Carnegie Mellon University

• Reduce risk before construction begins

• Catch gaps before they become RFIs
• Protect margins before the first shovel hits the ground
